info.name: Personal Search Assistant
info.description:
REST API for the Personal Search Assistant (Java 21 + Quarkus). Set the `baseUrl` collection variable to your running instance.

**App API** — Knowledge, Connections, Search, Indexing and Health cover every endpoint the app exposes (`api.resource.*` plus the SmallRye Health probes under `/q`).

**Outbound APIs the app calls** — the remaining folders are not the app; they are the third-party and infrastructure APIs it talks to, mirrored request-for-request so you can test each leg in isolation when something upstream breaks:
- *Google Auth* + *Connector Responses (raw Google API)* — Drive/Gmail ingestion. Run *Google Auth > Refresh access token* first to populate `googleAccessToken`.
- *Embedding Provider (raw)* — the hosted embedding call the indexing stage makes (`app.embedding.provider=openai-embed`).
- *LLM Provider (raw)* — the chat-completion call behind `answer: true` (`app.llm.provider=openai-compat`).
- *OpenSearch (chunk index)* — the queries `OpenSearchSearchIndex` issues against the `chunks` alias.

Provider base URLs, models and index names are collection variables defaulting to the values in `application.properties`; the api-key variables are blank on purpose — fill them from your `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `GROQ_API_KEY` and do not commit them.

request.description: Pages this knowledge's ingested entities, newest-first (updatedAt descending, id as tiebreak). Enable the optional ?status= query param to filter by EntityStatus (INGESTED, INDEXING, INDEXED, FAILED, DELETED); omit it for all. `limit` defaults to 50 and is clamped to 1..200; `offset` defaults to 0. The response is `{ items, total, limit, offset }` where `total` counts every match, not the page. Rows are projections — the raw source payload and the extracted body are never sent. An unknown status name or a negative offset is a 400; an unknown id is a 404.

This knowledge's ingestion cursors — one per (iterableId, direction), ordered for stable rendering. Each carries `iterableName`, the display name discover() gave that sub-stream (null on cursors created before names were stored — the next reconcile fills it in). The real sync-progress view: a BACKWARD cursor at EXHAUSTED means the backfill is complete, a FORWARD cursor at IDLE is waiting for its next scheduled run, SUSPENDED means the knowledge is paused, and RETIRED means the iterable disappeared at the source (its data is kept). The connector-internal `attributes` and the worker `lease` are deliberately not exposed. 404 on an unknown id.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "My Documents",
  "type": "LOCAL_FS",
  "connectionId": null,
  "auth": {},
  "inputs": { "rootPath": "/home/me/Documents" },
  "cron": null,
  "interval": null,
  "scheduleEnabled": true,
  "backfillEnabled": true,
  "chunkingStrategy": "recursive",
  "chunkingMaxSize": 1200,
  "chunkingOverlap": 150,
  "chunkingSeparators": ["\n\n", "\n", " ", ""],
  "retentionPeriod": null
}

request.description:
type is one of LOCAL_FS, GMAIL, SLACK, GOOGLE_DRIVE, NOTION, JOB_BOARDS.

connectionId names the Connection to authenticate through; null uses the type's default connection (ignored by no-auth connectors like LOCAL_FS and the ATS job boards). auth is an inline credentials fallback, normally omitted when a connection is used.

cron, interval, scheduleEnabled and backfillEnabled are optional. Leave both cron and interval null to inherit the connector default (LOCAL_FS = 1 day, JOB_BOARDS = 3 hours) then the global default; set one to override (cron wins if both are set).

chunkingStrategy is one of recursive, character, fixed-size, token. chunkingMaxSize is characters (or tokens for the token strategy), chunkingOverlap is the overlap in the same unit, and chunkingSeparators is the ordered separator list for recursive/character. Any chunking field left null/empty inherits the global default at index time.

retentionPeriod ages entities out, measured from createdAt (e.g. "14d"). null inherits: the connector default (JOB_BOARDS = 14 days), then the global app.retention.default-period, which ships BLANK. Unset at every tier means NEVER EXPIRE — that is what keeps a document corpus from deleting itself, so only feed-like sources age out.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "My Documents (renamed)",
  "inputs": { "rootPath": "/home/me/Documents" },
  "cron": null,
  "interval": "30m",
  "scheduleEnabled": true,
  "backfillEnabled": true,
  "webhookEnabled": false,
  "webhookSecret": null,
  "chunkingStrategy": "token",
  "chunkingMaxSize": 512,
  "chunkingOverlap": 64,
  "chunkingSeparators": null,
  "retentionPeriod": null
}

request.description:
Partial edit with patch semantics: a field that is absent (or JSON null) is left unchanged; only fields present with a value change.

Attempting to change the immutable type is a 400; editing a DELETED knowledge is a 409; an unknown id is a 404.

Note: because an omitted field and an explicit null both arrive as null, cron/interval here mean "unchanged" — they cannot be cleared back to inherit via this endpoint.

retentionPeriod is a config-class edit: it changes only what a later retention sweep removes, never what is ingested. Like cron/interval it cannot be cleared back to inherit here.

Which platform hosts each company, and how many postings its board holds — run this BEFORE the next request to build a companies list that is known to resolve.

Reach here is purely a function of how many companies you name, so this is the endpoint you spend time in: paste a batch of candidates, keep the ones that come back found.

Each name is probed against Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and SmartRecruiters in that order, first hit wins. A platform prefix (lever:cred) pins it and skips the probe. Workday is never probed — it cannot be derived from a bare name — so pass its full tenant/site/wd triple and it is verified directly.

found: false is a normal answer, not an error: it means none of the supported platforms has a board for that name. razorpay is in the sample body as a known example of one.

postings is the WHOLE board, before inputs.locations is applied. Expect the Indian share to be roughly a tenth of it — databricks came back 862 here and yields 92 after an India city filter.

These are live, sequential calls to someone else's APIs. Three names took about 30 seconds; the request is capped at 50 names (400 above that, and 400 on an empty list). Nothing is written — safe to re-run.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "India job boards",
  "type": "JOB_BOARDS",
  "connectionId": null,
  "auth": {},
  "inputs": {
    "companies": [
      "paytm",
      "meesho",
      "databricks",
      "sarvam",
      "lever:cred"
    ],
    "locations": [
      "India",
      "Bengaluru",
      "Bangalore",
      "Hyderabad",
      "Pune",
      "Mumbai",
      "Gurugram",
      "Noida",
      "Chennai",
      "Delhi"
    ]
  },
  "cron": null,
  "interval": null,
  "scheduleEnabled": true,
  "backfillEnabled": false,
  "chunkingStrategy": null,
  "chunkingMaxSize": null,
  "chunkingOverlap": null,
  "chunkingSeparators": null,
  "retentionPeriod": "14d"
}

request.description:
ONE knowledge for every company job board. inputs.companies takes company handles as they appear in the careers URL; Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and SmartRecruiters are all probed and the platform that hosts each company is resolved once at discovery and recorded on its iterable, so grab never re-probes.

Prefix an entry with a platform to pin it (lever:cred) — useful for a company mid-migration with boards on two platforms, where probe order would otherwise decide silently.

inputs.locations keeps only postings whose location matches one of the terms; omit it to keep every country. LIST THE CITIES, not just "India" — 27 of Stripe's 36 Indian roles are filed as plain "Bengaluru" with no country, so the country alone keeps 3 of 36. A posting with NO location always survives (unstated is not the same as irrelevant). This is a cost control more than a correctness one: Databricks is 857 postings for 92 Indian ones, and everything kept gets parsed, chunked and embedded.

backfillEnabled is false because this connector is FORWARD-ONLY: a job board has no history worth walking.

retentionPeriod is what removes closed postings — boards send no tombstone, a role just stops appearing. Leave it null to inherit the connector default of 14 days.

A company that resolves to no platform is skipped and logged; activation only fails if NONE of them resolve.

Check the response body for status: a failed activation returns HTTP 200 with status ERROR.

item.name: Connections
item.description: Reusable, per-account connections holding the credentials a knowledge authenticates through. Register several accounts of the same connector (e.g. two Gmail logins) and bind different knowledges to whichever they want; one connection per type is the default used when a knowledge names none.

request.description: Lists all connections. Enable the optional ?type= query param to filter by connector type (GMAIL, GOOGLE_DRIVE, SLACK, NOTION, LOCAL_FS). An unknown type value is a 400.

Verifies the credentials, then persists and assigns the type default. type is one of GMAIL, GOOGLE_DRIVE, SLACK, NOTION; a no-connection connector like LOCAL_FS (or bad creds) is a 400.

auth is opaque per-connector credentials (e.g. refreshToken/accessToken); config is opaque connector-level settings (e.g. an OAuth client), or null. The first connection of a type becomes its default; makeDefault forces it.

rateLimit caps the outbound calls made with this account. A call must satisfy EVERY rule, and each rule is a token bucket whose capacity is permits — so 500/60s already allows a 500-request burst on an idle bucket, and there is no separate burst setting. Omit the field to inherit app.ratelimit.connector.<TYPE>.rules, which ships blank (unlimited).

Partial edit with patch semantics: an absent (or null) field is left unchanged; type is immutable and not editable here. Changing auth triggers re-verification of the credentials (400 on failure). An unknown id is a 404.

Because absent means unchanged, REMOVING a rate limit takes an explicit empty list — {"rateLimit": {"rules": []}} — see "Clear connection rate limit". Sending null leaves the existing limit in place.

Removes this account's rate limit so the server-wide app.ratelimit.* default applies again.

An empty rules array is the ONLY way to say this: null means "leave unchanged" on every PATCH field, so it cannot also mean "clear".

Re-checks the STORED credentials against the connector and records the outcome on the connection.

Always 200 with the refreshed connection whether or not the check passed — read status (ACTIVE / ERROR) and lastError. A bad credential is a result to display, not a 4xx.

Credentials are otherwise only verified at create and on an auth edit, so a token that expires later leaves the connection reading ACTIVE while every sync fails. ConnectionHealthScheduler runs this automatically every app.connections.health-interval (30m); IngestionJob then SKIPS knowledges whose connection is in ERROR rather than failing on every tick.

A DISABLED connection stays DISABLED even if the check passes — that is an operator decision.
Make this connection the default for its type. An unknown id is a 404.
An unknown id is a 404; a connection still bound to one or more knowledges is a 409.

Only query is required — a blank or absent query is a 400, and an unknown mode is a 400 that names the valid ones. knowledgeIds empty/omitted searches all. mode is LEXICAL, SEMANTIC or HYBRID (default HYBRID). topK defaults to 10 and is clamped to app.search.max-top-k (100); it is multiplied by app.search.candidate-multiplier before becoming the OpenSearch size and knn k.

Set answer true to include a generated answer, which cites hits as [n] (1-based into hits). The answer is grounded in each hit's FULL chunk text within app.agent.context-chars; a source that had to be cut is marked "[…truncated]" in the prompt, so the model says what it could not see instead of reporting the missing part as absent from the source.

If the LLM is unavailable this returns 200 with the hits intact and answerError set — it no longer 500s and discards the results.

Each hit carries chunkId (<entityId>_<ordinal>, pinning the matched passage), knowledgeId (which source the hit came from) and ordinal (position within the entity) alongside entityId, title, snippet, uri, score and metadata. snippet is a display excerpt only, app.search.snippet-chars long and taken from the matching region when highlighting found one; the full chunk text grounds the answer but is not put on the wire.

Optional: maxChunksPerEntity caps how many chunks one entity may contribute (1 = one result per document), overriding app.search.max-chunks-per-entity for this request; collapseDuplicates groups near-identical hits and keeps one of each. Both default off. See the "Search job postings" example for range filters.

Filters resolve the map key verbatim as an OpenSearch field path, so any normalised posting facet works without server changes: metadata.company, metadata.location, metadata.remote, metadata.seniority, metadata.board, metadata.dedupeKey, metadata.compMin/compMax, metadata.compCurrency, metadata.postedAt.

CAUTION on comp: pair it with metadata.compCurrency or the filter is meaningless — compMin is a plain number, so 150000 reads as USD on one posting and INR on the next. And expect it to be absent: of 208 India-located postings sampled across these boards, 0 stated pay at all (US postings do, because several states require it). A comp filter excludes nearly every Indian role rather than narrowing it.

The VALUE decides the clause. A scalar is an exact term; a map carrying gte/gt/lte/lt is a range — which is the only way to say "posted in the last week" or "pays at least X". JSON types are preserved, so metadata.remote must be true and not "true": a string term against a boolean field matches nothing.

maxChunksPerEntity 1 returns one hit per posting instead of one per chunk of its description. collapseDuplicates groups the same role reached by different routes — identical text, then an equal metadata.dedupeKey, then high token overlap — and keeps the member with the highest metadata.sourceRank, so a direct board listing wins over an aggregator's. Both are off unless asked for.

Set knowledgeIds to a job-board knowledge to search postings alone.

item.name: Search by a document (find things like this)

body.raw:
{
  "query": "roles I could do next",
  "sourceEntityId": "{{entityId}}",
  "knowledgeIds": ["{{knowledgeId}}"],
  "filters": { "metadata.remote": true },
  "topK": 10,
  "mode": "HYBRID",
  "answer": false,
  "maxChunksPerEntity": 1,
  "collapseDuplicates": true
}

request.description:
Searches BY an already-ingested document instead of by typed text — "find everything like this". Set sourceEntityId to the entity id of, say, an indexed CV (find it via Knowledge > List knowledge entities).

The document is NOT used as the query. It is decomposed by the document-facets task into a few short queries written in the register of the corpus being searched, each is retrieved normally, and the rankings are fused — so a posting matching three facets outranks one that matches a single facet very well.

query stops being the search text here and becomes a statement of intent that steers the decomposition; it may be blank. Blank query AND no sourceEntityId is a 400.

Facets are cached by the source document's checksum, so editing and re-indexing it derives them again with nothing to invalidate. If the LLM is unavailable this falls back to the document's opening text as a single query rather than failing. A document over app.search.document-query.max-chars is a 400; an unknown sourceEntityId is a 404.
Every saved search, newest first. nextRunAt null means "due now" — a freshly created digest runs on the next scheduler tick rather than one whole interval later.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "New roles for me",
  "query": "roles I could do next",
  "sourceEntityId": "{{entityId}}",
  "knowledgeIds": ["{{knowledgeId}}"],
  "filters": { "metadata.remote": true },
  "window": "1d",
  "cron": null,
  "interval": "1d",
  "taskId": "job-fit",
  "topK": 10,
  "collapseDuplicates": true,
  "maxChunksPerEntity": 1,
  "onlyNew": true,
  "enabled": true
}

request.description:
A digest needs EITHER query OR sourceEntityId; neither is a 400. Everything else has a default.

window is how far back a run looks, applied as a range filter on the chunk's indexedAt. interval (or cron) is how often it runs, resolved by the same ScheduleResolver the ingestion schedulers use.

taskId names a task in config/prompts.json to run over the results — job-fit scores postings, or leave it null for results only.

onlyNew drops anything an earlier run already reported, keyed on the ENTITY (a chunk id changes when a document is re-chunked). That is what makes this a digest rather than a repeated search.

Set the digestId collection variable from the response to use the requests below.
One digest.

The only editable field. A paused digest is never scheduled but can still be run by hand — that is the difference between pausing and deleting.

Fuller editing is delete-and-recreate.

Runs immediately without waiting for the schedule, and returns the run.

A search or task failure comes back as a run carrying "error" rather than a 5xx — the run happened, it just failed. That is deliberate: a scheduled job that throws leaves no trace, and a digest broken for a week has to be visible in its history.

A failed run records no items, so it cannot suppress anything on the next run.

History, newest first. limit is capped at 100.

Runs are also how newness is computed, which is why they are kept rather than overwritten.
The most recent run. 404 if the digest has never run.
Deletes the digest and its whole run history. 204.
Returns { knowledgeId, cursorsArmed }.

Revives a knowledge's dead-lettered work: FAILED cursors -> AVAILABLE and FAILED entities -> INGESTED, both with a fresh retry budget. Cursor position is kept, so a revived cursor resumes where it stopped rather than re-walking the source.

It also releases any cursor still held by a rate limit (RATE_LIMITED -> AVAILABLE, hold cleared): that instant was computed against a quota you have typically just raised, so this is the only way to shorten a hold.

Distinct from *Trigger forward sync*: that one only re-arms FORWARD cursors sitting IDLE, so it can never revive a dead-lettered backward (backfill) cursor. Nothing else moves a cursor or entity out of FAILED.

Returns { knowledgeId, cursorsRetried, entitiesRetried }.

Queues every one of a knowledge's entities for re-indexing from STORED content — no re-fetch from the source. Returns {"queued": n}.

This is what makes changing the embedding model survivable. Same vector width does NOT mean compatible vectors: switching app.embedding.provider or app.embedding.openai.model leaves the corpus half old-model and half new, and semantic search degrades with no error anywhere. Run this for every knowledge after such a change.

Entities a worker currently holds a lease on are skipped rather than raced; call again once the lease lapses to pick them up.

item.name: Health
item.description: SmallRye Health endpoints exposed by Quarkus under the /q management root (quarkus-smallrye-health is a declared dependency). No app code registers these — they are extension-provided.

request.description: Aggregate of the started, live and ready groups. Returns { status: UP|DOWN, checks: [...] } — 200 when UP, 503 when DOWN. The MongoDB client extension contributes a readiness check here; OpenSearch is talked to over a plain REST client and is not health-checked.
Liveness group only — is the JVM up and not deadlocked. Does not touch Mongo or OpenSearch.
Readiness group — includes the MongoDB connection check. DOWN here usually means `docker compose up -d` was not run.
Startup group — whether startup observers (MongoIndexInitializer, OpenSearchIndexInitializer) have completed.

item.name: Google Auth
item.description: Helper to mint a short-lived Google access token from a refresh token, used by the raw Drive/Gmail requests below. These call Google directly, not the Personal Search Assistant app.

request.description: Exchanges a long-lived refresh token for a short-lived access token. Set googleClientId, googleClientSecret and googleRefreshToken first (the OAuth client must include the Drive/Gmail read scopes). The test script stores access_token into the googleAccessToken collection variable, which the raw Drive/Gmail requests use as their Bearer token.

item.name: Connector Responses (raw Google API)
item.description: Direct calls to Google's Drive & Gmail REST APIs that mirror exactly what the connectors send — same field subset, params and query shape — so you can inspect the raw responses the connectors parse and map. Run 'Google Auth > Refresh access token' first to populate {{googleAccessToken}}; every request in this folder inherits it as a Bearer token.

request.description:
Mirrors HttpDriveApi.listFiles: the exact field subset and shared-drive params the connector requests. Returns { files: [ { id, name, mimeType, modifiedTime, size, version, md5Checksum, webViewLink, trashed } ], nextPageToken }.

Adjust q to scope like the connector does, e.g. "'root' in parents and trashed=false and mimeType!='application/vnd.google-apps.folder'". Enable pageToken to fetch the next page. Copy an id into driveFileId for files.get / files.export.

Mirrors HttpDriveApi.download — raw bytes of a binary/blob file, which GoogleDriveConnector writes to app.ingestion.google-drive.download-dir and passes on as a fileRef (never as bytes, per the 16 MB Mongo cap). Fails for Google-native docs (Docs/Sheets/Slides); use files.export for those. Files larger than app.ingestion.google-drive.max-file-bytes (25 MB) are skipped by the connector.

Mirrors HttpDriveApi.export — converts a Google-native doc to an exportable type before ingestion. Set driveExportMimeType to the target: text/plain for Docs, text/csv for Sheets, application/pdf for Slides. Errors with 403 on a non-native (binary) file — those go through files.get?alt=media instead.

Mirrors HttpDriveApi.about — the credential-verification probe run by POST /api/connections for a GOOGLE_DRIVE connection. A 2xx here is exactly what makes connection creation succeed; a 401/403 is what surfaces as the 400 from that endpoint.

Mirrors HttpGmailApi.listMessages against users/me. Returns the lightweight { messages: [ { id, threadId } ], nextPageToken, resultSizeEstimate } — the id/threadId refs the connector then fetches individually. Repeat labelIds for multiple labels; enable q for a Gmail search predicate (the connector passes after:/before: here); enable pageToken to page. Copy an id into gmailMessageId for 'messages.get'.

Mirrors HttpGmailApi.getMessage (format=full). Returns the full message — id, threadId, labelIds, snippet, internalDate, historyId and the payload MIME tree with headers and base64url body parts — exactly what GmailConnector walks to build the searchable text. Set gmailMessageId from a messages.list result.

Mirrors HttpGmailApi.listLabels — the label catalogue the GMAIL connector turns into iterables (one cursor pair per label). Returns { labels: [ { id, name, type } ] }. Use the ids here as labelIds in messages.list and in the knowledge inputs.

Mirrors HttpGmailApi.getProfile — the credential-verification probe run by POST /api/connections for a GMAIL connection, and the source of the historyId that feeds the gmail:<id>;hist:<historyId> checksum. Returns { emailAddress, messagesTotal, threadsTotal, historyId }.

item.name: Job Board APIs (raw)
item.description:
The public job-board APIs behind the ATS connectors, called directly so you can inspect the raw JSON the connectors parse and map — same endpoints, same params.

All of these are PUBLIC AND KEYLESS except Adzuna: no Authorization header, no Connection required, which is why the ATS connectors override requiresConnection() to false.

Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby return a whole board in one response (snapshot-shaped, no pagination). SmartRecruiters and Workday are paginated and are NOT yet wired into connectors — they are here so you can evaluate them before the adapters are built.

Counts quoted in each request were measured on 2026-09-02 and will drift.

request.description:
Exactly what GreenhouseConnector.fetchBoard calls. content=true is what makes ONE call sufficient — without it you get job stubs and each description needs a second request.

The whole board comes back in a single response: no pagination, no updated_after. That is why these connectors are snapshot-shaped and implement SourceConnector directly rather than extending a paging base.

Fields the normaliser reads: id, title, updated_at (the change signal), first_published, absolute_url, company_name, location.name, content (HTML-escaped).

Try boards: groww, databricks, stripe, gitlab, inmobi, rubrik, mongodb.
One posting, for inspecting the full content HTML the parser and chunker receive. Take an id from the list call above. Not used by the connector — it is here for debugging a single posting's parse.

What LeverConnector.fetchBoard calls. mode=json returns structured postings rather than rendered HTML.

NOTE THE MISSING FIELD: Lever publishes createdAt but NO updated timestamp. A checksum built from createdAt alone would never move, so an edited posting would be skipped forever by change detection — the connector hashes the body as well. That is the one real difference between the three ATS connectors.

Fields read: id, text (title), createdAt (epoch millis), hostedUrl, categories.location/team/commitment, description (HTML), descriptionPlain.

Try sites: paytm (174 India roles), meesho, cred, zeta, mindtickle, nium. A site that does not exist returns 404 with {"ok":false}; an empty board returns [].

What AshbyConnector.fetchBoard calls. The richest of the three: includeCompensation=true returns STRUCTURED pay bands (compensation.summaryComponents with minValue/maxValue/currencyCode), which the connector prefers over scraping prose. isRemote is stated as a real boolean rather than inferred, and closedAt — when present — becomes Entity.expiresAt and beats the knowledge-level retention window.

Try boards: sarvam (62/62 India), tekion, snowflake, bureau, atlan, confluent.

PUBLIC AND KEYLESS — no auth header at all. Not yet wired into a connector; this is the platform proposed as the next adapter.

Paginated on limit/offset with totalFound, unlike the three boards above which return everything at once.

Measured: Swiggy 71 postings of which 70 are in India; Freshworks 162 of which 31. Both companies are absent from Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby — this platform is how they become reachable.

An unknown company returns 200 with totalFound: 0 and an empty content array, NOT a 404 — so a resolver must check totalFound, not the status code.

Full detail for one posting, including the job description sections the list call omits. Take an id from the list call above.

Relevant to the adapter design: if the list response lacks the description, ingestion needs one call per posting rather than one per company — check this before assuming the snapshot shape applies.

PUBLIC AND KEYLESS, but a POST with a JSON body — the existing AtsHttp helper only does GET, so this platform needs one new method.

Genuinely paginated: limit caps at 20 while tenants hold 200-300+, so a grab must loop on offset until it drains. Response carries total and jobPostings[] with title, locationsText and externalPath.

THE URL IS THE HARD PART. It needs a tenant + site + wd-number triple, and none of the three is guessable — 13 of 22 blind guesses failed even for companies that certainly use Workday (Accenture, Walmart, IBM, Visa, Qualcomm). Read the real URL off the company's careers page.

Verified triples: adobe/external_experienced/wd5 (133 India roles), nvidia/nvidiaexternalcareersite/wd5, salesforce/External_Career_Site/wd12, micron/External/wd1, mastercard/CorporateCareers/wd1, target/targetcareers/wd5, hpe/Jobsathpe/wd5.

A wrong site or wd number returns HTML or a 422, not a clean 404.

Server-side filtering to India, which would avoid ingesting the ~90% of a tenant's postings that are other countries.

IT IS NOT RELIABLE. That GUID is India on Adobe (returns 133 roles) but returns total: null on NVIDIA and Salesforce — the facet ids are not dependably cross-tenant. That is why the plan filters location client-side instead; this request is here so you can check whether a given tenant happens to support it.

To find a tenant's real facet ids, POST with an empty appliedFacets and read the facets[] block in the response.

AGGREGATOR, not an ATS — indexes postings copied from many sources rather than serving one company's own board. Needs a free API key from developer.adzuna.com; set adzunaAppId and adzunaAppKey.

The 'in' path segment is the India endpoint and is confirmed live: with dummy NON-EMPTY credentials it returns a clean {"exception":"AUTH_FAIL"} rather than a 404.

Leaving adzunaAppId/adzunaAppKey blank gives an HTML 400 instead, which looks like a broken request — put any placeholder value in both to see the real auth error.

Not implemented. It is tracked as the breadth option once the ATS platforms are in, and would be the first connector in the repo needing outbound rate limiting — nothing throttles HTTP today (PermitService caps lease concurrency, not request rate).

Paginates by page number in the PATH (.../search/1, /2, /3), which is why it would extend TokenWindowGrabber with the page number as the token rather than the snapshot base.

item.name: Embedding Provider (raw)
item.description: The hosted embedding API the indexing stage calls directly, over the OpenAI-compatible schema (OpenAiCompatibleEmbeddingProvider, app.embedding.provider=openai-embed). Defaults match application.properties: Gemini's OpenAI-compat endpoint with text-embedding-004. Set embeddingApiKey to your GEMINI_API_KEY. Point embeddingBaseUrl at http://localhost:11434/v1 to test an Ollama model instead — the app switches the same way, config only.

request.description:
Mirrors OpenAiCompatibleEmbeddingProvider.embedAll — one batched call per app.indexing.embed-batch (64) chunks. Returns { data: [ { index, embedding: [...] } ] }; the provider re-orders by `index`, so ordering from the API does not matter, but a data length != input length throws.

`dimensions` is app.embedding.openai.dimensions: gemini-embedding-001 is natively 3072, and this asks for the 768 prefix that fits the knn mapping. Delete the line to see the model's native width (that is what dimensions=0 does in the app).

The test script asserts the returned width equals embeddingDimension (768). A mismatch is the failure mode invariant 5 warns about: the width is baked into the OpenSearch knn_vector mapping at index creation, so a width you cannot request needs chunks_v2 + an alias flip, not just a config edit.

A 404 'Requested entity was not found' here means the model id no longer resolves — usually a retired model, not a bad key (a bad key is 400/403).

item.name: LLM Provider (raw)
item.description: The chat-completion API the search agent calls directly when a search is run with answer=true (OpenAiCompatibleLlmProvider, app.llm.provider=openai-compat). Defaults match application.properties: Groq with llama-3.3-70b-versatile. Set llmApiKey to your GROQ_API_KEY. If this folder fails, POST /api/search with answer=true 500s and loses its hits — the known async trap the console works around by retrying without the flag.

request.description: Mirrors OpenAiCompatibleLlmProvider.complete — the system prompt plus the numbered-hit user message DefaultSearchAgent builds, at app.llm.temperature (0.2). The provider reads choices[0].message.content and throws on an empty choices array, so this is the request to run when answers come back blank or the endpoint 500s.

Not called by the app — a cheap way to verify llmApiKey and llmBaseUrl and to confirm the exact model id to put in app.llm.model before a chat completion. Available on Groq, OpenAI and Ollama; a provider that lacks it is not a problem for the app.

item.name: OpenSearch (chunk index)
item.description: Direct calls to the OpenSearch instance from docker-compose (:9200) that mirror what OpenSearchSearchIndex and OpenSearchIndexInitializer send. Not the app's API — this is for inspecting what the indexing stage actually wrote. Code only ever talks to the `chunks` alias (physical index chunks_v2_768).

request.description: Single-node dev cluster reports status yellow (no replicas) — that is expected, not a fault.

The mapping OpenSearchIndexInitializer PUT at startup, including the `chunks` alias and the knn_vector `embedding` field. The `dimension` in that mapping is app.embedding.dimension frozen at index-creation time — check it here before switching embedding models (invariant 5).
How many chunks exist across all knowledges. The quickest check that stage 2 (Mongo -> OpenSearch) is actually running after a sync.

The exact body OpenSearchSearchIndex.lexicalSearch builds — multi_match over text+title, knowledgeIds as a terms filter, extra filters appended as term clauses on any indexed field. Use it to see raw _score and _source when a POST /api/search result looks wrong; the app's HYBRID mode fuses this with the knn variant via RRF, so scores here will not match the API's.

Swap the must clause for { "knn": { "embedding": { "vector": [...], "k": 10 } } } to reproduce vectorSearch — you need a real vector from the Embedding Provider folder.

Every chunk written for one entity, in ordinal order — the way to verify a chunking-config change after POST /api/index/entities/{id}/reindex. Chunk ids are <entityId>_<ordinal>; indexing is an idempotent delete-then-replace, so ordinals are always contiguous from 0.

Mirrors OpenSearchSearchIndex.deleteByEntity (conflicts=proceed), the first half of the idempotent replace. Prefer DELETE /api/index/entities/{id} — that keeps Mongo and the index in step, whereas this leaves the entity INDEXED in Mongo with no chunks behind it. Swap the term field to knowledgeId to reproduce deleteByKnowledge. OpenSearch is fully regenerable: a reindex rebuilds anything removed here.
